# firecrawl map

Discover URLs on a site. Use `--search` to find a specific page within a large site.

**Prerequisite:** `map` requires authentication (no keyless free tier); without credentials the CLI prompts an interactive login.

## Quick start

```bash
# Find a specific page on a large site
firecrawl map "<url>" --search "authentication" -o .firecrawl/filtered.txt

# Get all URLs
firecrawl map "<url>" --limit 500 --json -o .firecrawl/urls.json
```

Run `firecrawl map --help` for the full option list (sitemap handling, subdomains, etc.).

**Done when:** the URL list is saved under `.firecrawl/` and you have selected the URLs to scrape or crawl next.

## Tips

- **Map + scrape is a common pattern**: use `map --search` to find the right URL, then `scrape` it.
- Example: `map https://docs.example.com --search "auth"` → found `/docs/api/authentication` → `scrape` that URL.

## See also

- [firecrawl-scrape](../firecrawl-scrape/SKILL.md) — scrape the URLs you discover
- [firecrawl-crawl](../firecrawl-crawl/SKILL.md) — bulk extract instead of map + scrape
- [firecrawl-download](../firecrawl-download/SKILL.md) — download entire site (uses map internally)
- [firecrawl-build-search](https://github.com/firecrawl/skills/tree/main/skills/build/firecrawl-build-search) — building URL discovery into an app instead of running it here

The search returned several Supabase docs pages on Row Level Security (RLS). The main points:

- **Core model:** The Data API uses two layers. Grants decide which roles can reach an object, and RLS policies decide which rows those roles can touch. The securing-your-API guide says to use both for every exposed object (Supabase's "Securing your API" guide describes grants and RLS as two layers, with grants controlling role access and RLS policies controlling row access).
- **Enabling RLS:** Tables made in the Dashboard get RLS automatically, but tables created with SQL need it turned on manually. Until a policy exists, Data API requests return no rows. The tables guide also says to give every table a policy, even a permissive one.
- **Key roles:** Publishable keys map to the `anon` or `authenticated` roles, and policies are written against those roles. Secret keys map to `service_role`, which bypasses RLS, so they should stay on the server (Policies never apply to a secret key, because service_role has the BYPASSRLS attribute.).
- **Debugging:** A missing grant produces a permission error, while a policy that matches nothing returns an empty result, so check grants first.
- **Auth link:** RLS policies typically filter on `auth.uid()`. The Auth docs note that the Auth Token scopes database access on a row-by-row level when used along with RLS policies.
- **Production:** The production checklist advises enabling RLS on all tables before launch, because tables without reasonable policies let any client read and modify their data.
- **Other uses:** The docs also cover RLS on `realtime.messages` for private Realtime channels, and RLS for RAG/vector search permissions.

Main pages found: the Securing your API guide, the Tables and data guide, the API keys guide, the Auth guide, the Realtime Authorization guide, and the Production Checklist. The dedicated "Row Level Security" page was linked from several of these but did not appear in the results, so its full text was not retrieved.

Web search results for query: "supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security"

Links: [{"title":"Row Level Security","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/row-level-security"},{"title":"Authorization via Row Level Security","url":"https://supabase.com/features/row-level-security"},{"title":"row level security","url":"https://www.mintlify.com/supabase/supabase/security/row-level-security"},{"title":"how to write row level security policies in supabase","url":"https://www.rapidevelopers.com/supabase-tutorial/how-to-write-row-level-security-policies-in-supabase"},{"title":"# How to Write Row Level Security Policies in Supabase","url":"https://www.rapidevelopers.com/md/supabase-tutorial/how-to-write-row-level-security-policies-in-supabase"},{"title":"supabase rls policies tutorial","url":"https://chat2db.ai/resources/blog/supabase-rls-policies-tutorial"},{"title":"Implementing Row-Based Permissions in Supabase Postgres","url":"https://www.getgalaxy.io/learn/glossary/implementing-row-based-permissions-in-supabase-postgres"},{"title":"what is rls and why it matters","url":"https://unpwned.io/qa/supabase/what-is-rls-and-why-it-matters"},{"title":"supabase security basics","url":"https://mcp.directory/skills/supabase-security-basics"}]

The search didn't return the exact page you named (`supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security`). The closest official result is the Supabase Auth guide at `supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/row-level-security`, which covers the core points:

- **Enabling RLS:** It must be turned on for tables in exposed schemas, which by default means `public`. Tables made in the dashboard Table Editor get it automatically, but tables created with raw SQL need it enabled manually. RLS must always be enabled on any tables stored in an exposed schema. By default, this is the public schema.
- **Policies:** Policies are SQL logic that you attach to a Postgres table. You can attach as many policies as you want to each table.
- **Auth helpers:** Supabase provides some helpers that simplify RLS if you're using Supabase Auth.
- **Example:** The guide shows a `SELECT` policy that grants public read access to a `profiles` table, with an alternative for limiting users to their own rows.

Other results add context. The Supabase feature page says policies can cover SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE, and that service keys or roles with the bypassrls privilege can skip them. A third-party tutorial (RapidDev, last updated March 2026) notes that without policies, RLS blocks all access. Those third-party sources are less authoritative than the official docs, so check them against Supabase's own documentation.
